name: Harbour docks
desc: The working edge of the water, where things and people arrive and leave without ceremony.
tags: harbour dockside, container gantry cranes, stacked shipping containers, mooring bollards, thick mooring ropes, concrete quayside, cargo ship hull, oily water, gulls, rusted railings, floodlight masts
prose: a working dockside of stacked shipping containers under gantry cranes, mooring ropes running from bollards to the rusted hull of a cargo ship lying in oily water
note: Splits two ways from the same word - a container terminal (cranes, stacks, floodlight masts) or an old fishing harbour (wooden posts, small boats, nets, low sheds). Pick one in the tags or you get an incoherent blend of both. The water has to be named as a surface, oily and still or choppy, otherwise the quay just ends at a blank edge and the sense of depth goes with it.
